For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

sugestoes.texto:
WHAT: The new member routes `delete "members"` / `put "members"` inside `resources :groups` expose the group id under `:id`, but the target actions read `params.require(:group_id)`.
WHY: Bare routes inside a `resources` block are member routes, so the path is `/admin/groups/:id/members` (param `:id`), while `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member` (groups_controller.rb:66, :85) do `params.require(:group_id)`. `:group_id` is never supplied, so every real `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/<id>/members.json` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400 — the add/remove-member feature is broken. The specs pass `group_id:` directly to xhr, bypassing routing, so they don't catch it.
HOW: Either change the routes to include the key, e.g. `delete ":group_id/members" => "groups#remove_member"` / `put ":group_id/members" => "groups#add_members"`, or make the controller read `params.require(:id)`.

WHAT: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members / limit 50 → 3 pages for only 2 real pages).
WHY: On the true last page `currentPage` (2) never equals `totalPages` (3), so `showingLast` stays false, the `next` action stays enabled, and clicking it sets `offset` to `user_count` and renders an empty page while the UI shows a non-existent page 3.
HOW: Use a ceiling division, e.g. `return Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"));`.

WHAT: remove_member passes a bare integer (`user_id`) to `group.users.delete(...)`, but `users` is a `has_many :through` collection whose `delete(*records)` expects associated record objects, not primary keys. WHY: unlike `destroy`, `delete` does not coerce numeric ids (see admin/users_controller.rb:128, which correctly passes `@user`), so this raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` and returns a 500 without removing the member (or, if unhandled by the association, deletes the wrong row). HOW: load the record first — `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` — or reuse the existing model helper `group.remove(User.find(user_id))` (group.rb:276), which deletes the group_users join row.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
`add_members` runs one User query per username; load all users with a single `User.where(username: ...)` query.

sugestoes.texto: The whole cancel loop is wrapped in one try/catch, so if a single `client.request` (SendGrid cancel) rejects for one reminder, the catch swallows it and every remaining reminder in `remindersToCancel` is skipped — never cancelled at SendGrid and never deleted from the DB. Impact: those workflow emails are still delivered even though the booking was cancelled/rescheduled, which is exactly the bug this PR intends to fix. Fix: move the try/catch inside the loop so one failed reminder does not abort cancellation of the others (and consider collecting the DB deletions to retry).

The async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls are invoked inside `forEach` without awaiting (the previous code awaited `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`), so the cancellation/flagging of reminders is fire-and-forget and the handler can return before it completes. Impact: reminders may remain scheduled and their emails still sent if the process ends before the pending promises settle. Fix: collect the returned promises and `await Promise.all(...)` before responding.

The new `immediateDelete` branch sends the SendGrid cancel request and `return`s without deleting the `workflowReminder` row. Unlike the `!referenceId` branch (deletes) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (always deletes), the row is left behind; in handleNewBooking's reschedule path (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`) the original booking is only set to CANCELLED and nothing cascades, so stale workflowReminder rows persist indefinitely. Impact: orphaned reminder records accumulate. Fix: delete the reminder row (in addition to cancelling the SendGrid send) in the immediateDelete branch.

The workflow-reminder cancellations for the previous rescheduled booking are invoked fire-and-forget inside `forEach` and are never awaited; the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch them because `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` swallow their own errors internally. Because the handler does not await these promises, in a serverless Next.js function the response can be sent (and the process frozen/terminated) before the SendGrid `POST /scheduled_sends` cancel and the DB writes complete, so the old booking's reminder emails can still be delivered — the exact behavior this PR is meant to fix. Await the operations (e.g. collect them into an array and `await Promise.all([...])`) instead of calling them inside `forEach`.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.descricao: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `tu` may be nil when no TopicUser row exists for the user/topic, yet `tu.notification_level` is dereferenced immediately. WHY: A user who receives a topic notification email but has no TopicUser record for that topic (e.g. category/mailing-list delivery before ever visiting) will trigger a NoMethodError (500) on `nil.notification_level`, breaking the unsubscribe link. HOW: Use `tu = TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` (or `TopicUser.change(...)`) so a missing row is handled/created instead of dereferenced.

WHAT: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's notification state via an unauthenticated-by-token, CSRF-unprotected GET (added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` and registered as a `get` route). WHY: A state change performed on a GET with no CSRF token can be forged cross-site (e.g. an `` or any fetch) against a logged-in victim, silently muting/unsubscribing them from a topic. HOW: Require a per-user signed token in the unsubscribe URL (like the digest `email_unsubscribe_url(key:)`) and verify it before mutating, or perform the mutation only via a POST/PATCH that carries the CSRF token.

WHAT: When the TopicUser row exists but its `notification_level` column is NULL, `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` raises (NoMethodError: undefined method `>' for nil). WHY: `TopicUser`'s own `tracking` scope uses `COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular)` (app/models/topic_user.rb:8-12), which is evidence the column can be NULL on persisted rows; any such row hitting this action returns a 500 instead of unsubscribing. HOW: read the level defensively, e.g. `level = tu.notification_level || TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` and compare/assign from `level`.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

issues.descricao: The topic unsubscribe GET endpoint is not idempotent: each visit steps the notification level down again, so reloading the link moves a topic from regular to muted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called with an empty data object, so no column is written and Prisma's `@updatedAt` hook never fires on SelectedCalendar. WHY: the call is a complete no-op — the comment and the intended 'update updatedAt for all calendars under this credential' side effect silently never happen (Prisma only applies @updatedAt when at least one field changes; updateMany with `data: {}` writes nothing). HOW: pass an explicit field write/assignment so a real change is made (e.g. set a concrete column, or explicitly assign `updatedAt: new Date()` / a counter column) instead of `{}`.

The only concrete defect anchored is the already-recorded empty-`data` updateMany call on CalendarService.ts:1024. It is one unconditional updateMany per fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache call and shares the same root cause/line as the already-recorded empty-data finding.

issues.descricao: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object, so Prisma does not refresh the @updatedAt timestamp and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never reflects the cache refresh.
issues.textoGolden: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

Comment claims "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" but call passes empty object {} as data, so nothing is updated (Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op/error). Fix comment or pass { updatedAt: new Date() } to match the stated intent.

updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {}. Prisma updateMany throws when data is empty, so this line throws on every resync after the cache write. Pass an explicit touch e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } instead of {}.

issues.descricao: After deleting the calendar cache, CredentialActionsDropdown does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so where no parent refetch callback is passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, while the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`. WHY: the 'Cache Status' row in the dropdown is rendered from the cached `connectedCalendars` result; after deleting the cache the query is not refetched, so the deleted status/last-updated entry stays visible and stale in the UI. HOW: invalidate the query in the cache-deletion mutation as well, e.g. `const utils = trpc.useUtils(); onSuccess: async () => { ...; await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }`.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only calls onSuccess?.() and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation onSettled. WHY: cacheUpdatedAt stays stale after deletion so UI keeps showing old Last updated and delete action until manual refetch. HOW: add onSettled invalidate of connectedCalendars like disconnect does.

Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

issues.descricao: The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale instead of the user's locale, so non-US users see US-style dates in an otherwise translated label.
issues.textoGolden: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

comentarios.texto: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)), so every user — regardless of their locale — sees a US-style date/time while the surrounding label is translated. Use the app's locale-aware date formatting helper (the user's current locale) instead of pinning en-US.

Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

issues.descricao: The calendar cache migration keeps a generated warning saying updatedAt has no default and cannot be added to a non-empty table, although the SQL adds it with DEFAULT NOW().

comentarios.texto: This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

issues.descricao: The test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0, including when called from the failure paths, so the script reports success when the tunnel could not be set up.

comentarios.texto: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

issues.descricao: The webhook test script updates .env with the macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on Linux GNU sed and leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged.
issues.textoGolden: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form. WHY: under GNU sed (typical Linux dev/CI environment) the empty `''` is consumed as the script operand and the command errors, so the existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line is never replaced and the tunnel URL is not written to the env file. HOW: use a portable invocation, e.g. `sed -i.bak -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` (or branch on `uname`).

The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.

When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

issues.descricao: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC returns a 500 instead of a structured FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error.
issues.textoGolden: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

issues.descricao: connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of the feature-flag-aware factory, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.
The dev script writes tunnelmole output to a fixed /tmp/tmole.log, so a local attacker's symlink at that path could make it overwrite an arbitrary file.

The new test-gcal-webhooks.sh writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to '../.env' relative to the current directory, so running it from the repo root creates/edits a .env above the repo and the app never sees the URL.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `should_block?` mutates persistent state (increments match_count, sets last_match_at, saves) while being used purely as a predicate from EmailValidator#validate_each (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13), which runs on every ActiveModel validation of the email attribute. WHY: validation is not idempotent — every call to `User#valid?` (including dry validations, repeated validations, and client retries of a blocked signup) performs a DB write and inflates match_count/last_match_at, so the "how many times each email was blocked" statistic is unreliable and the validation path silently gains write load. HOW: move the stat update out of the predicate — have `should_block?` only read `action_type`, and perform the increment/last_match_at update explicitly at the single call site that actually blocks a signup (e.g. in the validator after the error is added, or in the controller), so validation stays pure.

WHAT: `record.save`'s return value is ignored and the exception path is not handled. WHY: if the UPDATE fails (e.g. a uniqueness/validation error or a DB error), the match_count/last_match_at change is silently discarded with no signal, so block telemetry is lost without any indication; the method still proceeds to evaluate `record.action_type` from the in-memory object. HOW: check the result (`record.save` and handle/raise on failure, or use `update_columns(match_count: record.match_count, last_match_at: ...)` which skips validations and raises on failure) so a failed stat update is not swallowed.

`should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves on every invocation, but the signup path validates the user twice per attempt (UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` at app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168 and then `user.save` at line 172, which re-runs validations). Since EmailValidator invokes `BlockedEmail.should_block?` on each validation, a single blocked signup attempt increments `match_count` and `last_match_at` twice, so the 'number of times each email is blocked' statistic is inflated (≈2x) and the last-blocked timestamp is overwritten within the same request. Fix: perform the match-count/last_match_at update once per actual signup attempt outside the validation path (or guard against re-entry per request), rather than inside the validator.

issues.descricao: When the server rejects an email, the signup form marks it with the generic 'invalid email' text instead of the server's reason (blocked or not allowed).

comentarios.texto: The message shown for a rejected email disagrees with the reason the code is reacting to. This branch fires when the server rejected the email (result.errors.email), and this PR gives that condition its own server string — user.email.blocked, added in config/locales/server.en.yml as "is not allowed." — but the client re-labels it with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). A user whose address is perfectly well-formed but blocked/hosted on a blacklisted domain is therefore told their email is invalid, contradicting the reason just returned by the server. Use the blocked/not-allowed message (and add a matching client locale key) instead of user.email.invalid. Notice the same generic string is used at line ~94 for validation failures, so it should not be reused to represent a distinct server-side rejection.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match and no normalisation, so changing the letter case of a blocked address bypasses the block list.
issues.textoGolden: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

comentarios.texto: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.
Case-sensitivity bypass: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is exact case-sensitive with no normalization, while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and lookup.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count and last_match_at as a side effect of email validation, so each signup attempt (validated twice) inflates the counter and concurrent updates can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: should_block? mutates match_count/last_match_at via read-modify-write save inside a validator. WHY: Every validation call (including re-validations of the same attempt or attempts failing on unrelated fields like username) inflates stats, and concurrent signups lose increments with no atomic update. HOW: Move stats update out of validation or use atomic increment (update_counters/increment_counter) only on actual blocked rejections.

WHAT: `should_block?` mutates state (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, calls `record.save`) inside a method that is invoked from the model validation callback, and the signup controller runs validation twice per attempt (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168 then `user.save` at :172). WHY: a single signup attempt increments `match_count` twice and rewrites `last_match_at`, so the per-email block statistics the feature was built to track are wrong. HOW: make the read side non-mutating for validation and record the match separately (e.g. move the increment out of validation, or guard it so it runs once per attempt), keeping the predicate pure.

WHAT: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock or unique constraint protection. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` and one write overwrites the other, losing counts, so the tracked statistics drift under load. HOW: use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or a database-level counter increment.

issues.descricao: Claims the 'returns false' spec cannot distinguish nil from false because be_false is a truthiness matcher.

comentarios.texto: This test is named "returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist," but it cannot verify that. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]`, which yields `nil` (not `false`) when no record exists, and under this suite's RSpec 2 semantics `subject.should be_false` is a truthiness matcher that passes for any falsy value including `nil`. The assertion therefore passes on the nil the code actually returns and would only fail on an outright `true`; it does not pin the `false`/`nil` distinction its name asserts. Assert the value exactly (e.g. `subject.should == false`, or `be_falsey`/`be_nil` if nil is intended) so a regression returning a non-false falsy value is caught.

issues.descricao: The domain whitelist/blacklist regex @(domains) is not anchored at the end, so an address like user@example.com.evil.com matches a whitelist entry for example.com and bypasses the restriction.
issues.textoGolden: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: email_in_restriction_setting? builds unanchored Regexp "@(domains)" with only '.' escaped. WHY: Whitelist 'gmail.com' substring-matches 'victim@gmail.com.evil.com', so an attacker registers with an unapproved domain and bypasses the allow-list; blacklist similarly over/under-matches and other regex metachars are unescaped. HOW: Anchor and escape domains (e.g. Regexp.escape per domain split on '|' plus /\A[^@\s]+@(?:domain)\z/i).

issues.descricao: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.
A spec comment says last_match_at shows whether an email has ever been blocked, but should_block? updates it on every match, including do_nothing records.

sugestoes.texto: The added logging uses `r.log.Error(...)` for normal/expected outcomes, including dumping the entire `ids` slice, and passes the already-nil `err` from the preceding successful fetchIDs as the "err" value. Informational/success events are emitted at Error severity and the `ids` array can be tens of thousands of entries at large batch sizes, flooding error logs and tripping error-based alerting/monitoring. Additionally, logging the full `ids` slice at Error level every cycle compounds log/I-O volume.

Changed ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. `Run` invokes `clean()` on every tick, and `clean()` runs the entire cleanup job list (temp files, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history), each with a 9-minute timeout. Running it every minute instead of every 10 minutes raises cleanup DB/CPU load ~10x and, because `clean()` can run up to 9 minutes, effectively back-to-back. This is unrelated to the stated deadlock fix and looks like a debug leftover.

WHAT: The SQLite fallback builds the ID list with repeated `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop, which re-copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration (O(N^2)).
WHY: With the batch sizes this path exists for (the accompanying test uses 32767 IDs, and `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is operator-configurable), this performs hundreds of millions of fmt/format-and-copy operations per batch in the cleanup job, turning a linear join into a quadratic hot spot.
HOW: Build the values once with a `strings.Builder` (or `strings.Trim(strings.Join(...))`), e.g. write the first ID then `b.WriteString(", ")` + `strconv.FormatInt(v, 10)` for the rest, then interpolate `b.String()` into the DELETE.

issues.descricao: Leftover debug logs in the annotation cleanup emit Error-level entries with the full ID list on every batch, flooding error logs during normal operation.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls r.log.Error on every cleanup batch (also duplicated at lines 554-557 and 576-579) dumping full ids slice, cond, and nil err at Error level. WHY: Fires Error-level log per batch and serializes up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs (32767 in new test), spamming error logs/monitoring on every normal cleanup run. HOW: Downgrade to Debug or remove; do not log full ids at Error.

WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` (and the identical Error-level logs for 'by count' and 'Tags to clean', lines 554/557/576/579) run on every batch in production. WHY: These log the full ID slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 elements) at Error severity on every cleanup iteration, flooding logs with false error noise and large payloads for a normal successful operation, and can trigger error-based alerting. HOW: Remove these log lines, or downgrade to Debug and drop the full `ids` slice (log only the count).

Avoid using Error-level logging on the normal cleanup path. The new r.log.Error calls emit count, ids, cond, and err at lines 534/537, 554/557, and 576/579 during non-error execution, creating log noise; consider downgrading or removing these logs on the normal path.

issues.descricao: The comment states SQLite's parameter limit is 999, which is only true for SQLite versions before 3.32.0.

comentarios.texto: The comment states that SQLite has a parameter limit of 999, but SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults to 32766 (as the added integration test also recognizes). This branch is choosing a conservative compatibility threshold, not expressing the limit of every SQLite database. Document 999 as the older-version/compatibility threshold so maintainers do not mistake this constant for the actual limit on modern SQLite.

issues.descricao: On MySQL and Postgres, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID without limit, so a cleanup batch size above 65535 makes every DELETE fail.

comentarios.texto: The bind-parameter workaround only handles SQLite's limit; the placeholder branch is used for every other engine with len(ids) placeholders and no bound. The previous implementation had no bind parameters, so this path is new. Postgres (extended protocol) and MySQL both cap bind parameters at 65535, so a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize larger than that makes this DELETE fail at Exec with a parameter-limit error instead of cleaning anything. Clamp the number of ids per DELETE (e.g. chunk into <=1000/<=65535 id sub-batches) for all dialects, not just SQLite.

On Postgres and MySQL, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID with no cap. A configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above the driver's bind-parameter limit (65535) makes every cleanup batch fail, and the cleanup job then never finishes. Split the IDs into chunks below the limit, or inline the integer IDs as the SQLite branch does.

issues.descricao: The SQLite inline ID list is built with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is quadratic in batch size.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: SQLite large-batch IN-list built with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. WHY: Quadratic string copying on large batches (e.g. 32767 IDs in added test) during cleanup, a background job path. HOW: Build with strings.Builder or strings.Join.

The SQLite literal-ID path rebuilds the entire accumulated string for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32,767 setting in the integration test, generate substantial repeated copying and allocation before each delete, consuming cleanup time and memory. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once.

issues.descricao: The cleanup service ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running every cleanup job ten times as often and increasing database load.
issues.textoGolden: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no justification. WHY: Runs all 8 cleanup jobs including the new multi-query (SELECT+DELETE per batch) annotation cleanup 10x more often, multiplying DB load. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or justify the frequency change separately.

WHAT: The cleanup job ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. WHY: This runs all cleanup jobs (annotations, expired snapshots/versions/images, short URLs, query history) 10× more frequently, multiplying background DB load and lock contention — the opposite of the deadlock mitigation this PR targets — and appears to be a debug leftover unrelated to the described change. HOW: Restore the ticker to `time.Minute * 10`.

The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job runs. This job also drives the annotation/tag cleanup path changed in this PR, which now fetches ID batches into memory and emits Error-level logs per batch, so running it every minute substantially increases DB load and log volume with no functional benefit. Unless a 1-minute cadence is explicitly intended, this should stay at 10 minutes (it reads like a leftover from testing).

issues.descricao: The 'running the max count delete again' test case no longer runs cleanup a second time after the PR's per-subtest seeding and cleanup, so it does not verify that a repeated max-count cleanup deletes nothing.
The annotation cleanup loop stops on a batch whose IDs were already deleted by a concurrent cleaner, leaving the remaining work to the next cycle; checking the fetched count instead would avoid that.
MaxCount annotation cleanup reads victim IDs with LIMIT/OFFSET and deletes them in a separate non-atomic statement, so concurrent deletions can make it delete annotations that should be retained.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getLoginPredicate() now adds 'idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))', but this shared SPI predicate is also consumed by IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() (services/.../IdentityProviderBean.java:226). WHY: That predicate is applied in getFederatedIdentityProviders() to the aliases of the user's already-linked federated identities, so any IDP linked to an organization whose BROKER_PUBLIC is not "true" is now silently filtered out of the linked/federated IDP list shown at login/account-linking — a behavioral regression for a caller that has nothing to do with the login-cache invalidation this clause was added for. HOW: Keep the login-availability clause out of the shared SPI predicate; either add a dedicated predicate (e.g. getLoginCachePredicate()) used only by the Infinispan invalidation code, or have IdentityProviderBean use the original enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin predicate.

WHAT: remove() now calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally at line 100, whereas the original code only performed the delegate lookup inside the isInvalid() branch. WHY: When the alias cache entry is valid (the common case), this adds an extra JPA/DB read on every identity-provider removal that the else branch already satisfies from the cached CachedIdentityProvider. HOW: Only fetch the stored model when it is actually needed, e.g. call idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) lazily inside the isInvalid branch (and reuse the cached model in the else branch for the login invalidation as well).

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.
remove() always queries idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias), adding a database lookup on every IDP removal even when the cached entry already holds the model.

sugestoes.texto: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the cached group's delegate can no longer be resolved, but the SPI contract documents that this method must never return null (GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount Javadoc: "Never returns null"; the JPA adapter always returns a long). Any caller that unboxes the result (e.g. arithmetic or comparison on the Long) will NPE at the caller instead of the previous NPE here, and any code assuming a non-null count now receives null. Return a non-null value (e.g. 0L) when the model is absent to preserve the contract.

The background reader thread loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` with no backoff and is terminated only by `deletedAll.set(true)`, which is executed after the delete loop with no try/finally. If any `group(uuid).remove()` call throws, the flag is never set and the non-daemon thread busy-loops forever, hanging the JVM/test suite. Wrap the deletion in try/finally to always set deletedAll (and/or mark the thread daemon and join/interrupt it) so a failed delete cannot leave the thread running.

issues.descricao: The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new raw conditions interpolate a JavaScript number array into `= ANY(${teamIds})` / `= ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (and `= ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` at line 201) without any cast. WHY: Prisma binds JS numbers as INT8 while the `teamId`/`userId` columns are int4, and the documented Prisma caveat is that array parameters used with `ANY` may need an explicit cast to the column type; otherwise the generated `= ANY($1)` can fail at runtime with a type/operator mismatch for org- and team-scoped queries — paths that the only executing test (user scope in getBaseConditions) does not cover. HOW: cast the parameter to the column type, e.g. `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}::int[])` (and likewise for the userId arrays).
The only behavioral delta is the SQL-text representation and the = ANY(array) interpolation, which is the already-reported finding.

getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql (NOTHING_CONDITION or real), never null, so authConditions is always truthy and the AND-combine always runs; the else-if/else branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable dead code.

Exact-array-order assertions in the test hunk depend on unordered DB result sets (findAllByParentId/findAllByTeamIds have no orderBy); this pre-existing order sensitivity was not made worse by this PR.

issues.descricao: In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

issues.descricao: The caching tests for getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions were removed in the Prisma.sql conversion, leaving the cached-condition logic untested.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The reschedule handler changed the loop callback from `(bookingRef) => {` to `async (bookingRef) => {`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the returned promises are discarded.
